title: Guided pilot config deployer for Optimize recommendations
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a guided pilot deployer that can safely auto-apply Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, prefix/KV caching profiles, and lightweight config tweaks) with enforceable gates, canary slices, automatic rollback triggers, and an approval workflow. The pilot deployer should be non-destructive by default, support manual override for operators, and emit rich audit events for Console and customer logs.

Scope: prototype and ship a safe-by-default orchestrator used by Optimize to push configuration changes to serving fleets for hosted and dedicated customers. This ticket covers the control-plane changes, canary routing interface, and an initial set of safety checks and rollback policies. It does NOT include full RBAC for enterprise Private installs (follow-up ticket planned).

Design highlights and constraints:
- Canary slices are policy-driven: by default 1% -> 10% -> 50% staged ramp with configurable hold durations. Canary routing leverages existing smart-routing primitives.
- Safety signals: latency p50/p95 regressions, 5xx increase, token cost delta, and quality regressions measured against a small eval prompt set (baseline pass rate). Thresholds are configurable per recommendation class.
- Rollback triggers: automated rollback when any critical signal crosses configured thresholds for N consecutive windows, or when a bespoke quality regression detector flags divergence.
- Approval model: two paths: (1) fully automated pilot where system proceeds through stages if checks pass, and (2) manual-gated pilot where a named approver must sign off before progressing to production. All approvals generate immutable audit events.
- Observability: emit per-stage tracing, per-key cost/latency deltas, and a compact human-readable report for Console and Slack alerts.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to ship):
1) A working pilot deployer service that accepts Optimize suggestions and performs staged application according to policy.
2) Canary routing implemented and tested end-to-end against a dedicated test pool.
3) Safety check subsystem running with configurable thresholds and acting on signals to pause/rollback.
4) Approval flow integrated (manual approve/deny) with audit log entries visible in Console.
5) E2E QA plan and a runbook for incident recovery documented.
6) Demo + docs (Confluence + Console walkthrough) produced for SRE/SEs.

Out of scope: full enterprise RBAC sync, offline on-prem upgrade path, automatic model-variant fallback for incompatible quantized builds (separate follow-up).

Notes on implementation approach: prefer reuse of existing route slicing and telemetry collectors. Introduce a lightweight policy engine (rule DSL) that maps suggestion types to default canary profiles and safety thresholds. Store pilot state in the standard deployment store so rollbacks are consistent with current rollout tooling.
